# Sahil Mittal {.hero-name}

[Interested in Labor Economics, Transit and Education Policy]{.hero-tagline}

I am a first-year MS in Public Policy and Management (Data Analytics) student at Carnegie Mellon University's Heinz College, studying economics, programming, Data Science and policy analysis. Interested in labor economics, transit and education policy. 

I spent four years at Plaksha University, a new age university in India, trying to reimagine technology education in India.
Two years went into building the inaugral Office of Corporate Partnerships and Careers
from nothing — strategy, operations and employer relationships for 700+ students. The last year was in the
Vice Chancellor's office, on institutional strategy, finanical modeling, cross-department projects and applied governance
projects with Invest Punjab.

Along with this I spent my time as Teaching Fellow for various courses at Plaksha teaching both undergraduate and Graduate students. I have background in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, with a minor in Physics. After engineering, I did Young India Fellowship at Ashoka University, spending a year studying various courses across History, Philosophy, Economics, Public Policy and Liberal Arts.

#### MBTA equity corridors

Ranked every MBTA bus route by transit dependence weighted by ridership, then
built the cost-benefit case for a $6.5M bus-priority package. Second place at the
MIT Policy Hackathon.

absorbs the shock of major life transitions while nonfiction holds steady.

## Learning to disagree well {.section-heading}

::: {.split}

::: {.split-media}
![](/images/bridge-cohort.jpg){.rounded-photo fig-alt="Inaugural BRIDGE cohort at the kickoff session"}
[Inaugural BRIDGE cohort at the kickoff session, University of Pittsburgh, September 2026.]{.photo-caption}
:::

::: {.split-text}
I am a participant in the BRIDGE Program, an eight-month co-curricular fellowship at Carnegie Mellon's Heinz College, 
built on the college's Deliberative Discourse Initiative and its partnership with the University of Pittsburgh School of Public and International Affairs. 
The program combines workshops, experiential learning, and collaborative projects to build practical capacity in civil discourse, dialogue facilitation, mediation, conflict management, and civic leadership. 
For me, it is a natural complement to my policy coursework: the analytical side of the degree tells you what a policy does, 
while BRIDGE is about the harder work of getting people with real disagreements into a room and keeping the conversation productive. That skill set feels increasingly central to whether evidence-based policy actually gets adopted. 
:::

:::

## Teaching {.section-heading}

::: {.prose}
My interest in education policy started in the classroom. 
Teaching showed me how much education shapes social mobility and how much of that potential is limited by conditions no individual controls. I moved toward policy to work on those conditions directly.
:::
